what_happened: The person running Athena closed queued item 487a by hand. It was Hestia's third re-queue of a request on paused line 5389, and it had stopped drain-44. The same paused-line item had already stopped three drains in one day. The the person running Athena then queued 20261031-184832-4gah so the drain skips items on paused lines. They raised 0hmz (Hestia must not re-queue requests a person has closed) to high priority. They also corrected the reading of 17c3, which used a banned word and said "create" where the work was "modify". No job failed. This was an intervention that overrode the drain's normal behavior.
cause: The drain treats every queued item as runnable and does not check the state of the line the item belongs to. A scope-guard pause on a line is therefore invisible to the drain. Hestia, the re-queuer, does not record that a person closed a request. It can put the same request back, and each re-queue meets the same pause. Nothing retires or revalidates an item whose line is paused, so one stale item can halt the whole queue repeatedly until a person intervenes. The reading slip on 17c3 (banned word, create vs modify) is a separate small case of a reading not being checked against writing rules and repo state.
prevention: Two code checks together. (1) Before dispatching an item, the drain checks the item's line. If the line is paused, it skips the item, records a visible "skipped: line paused" reason, and continues with the rest of the queue. A skipped item never counts as a failure and never stops the drain. (2) Queue admission and Hestia's re-queue path refuse any request that a person has closed, unless a person explicitly reopens it. Both checks must have tests that use a paused line and a person-closed item.
proposed_request: Make the queue drain robust to paused lines and person-closed requests. Outcome: (1) When drain picks the next item, it skips any item whose line is paused by the scope guard. It logs a "skipped: line paused" reason that `athena status` shows. It continues with the next item. A skipped item does not count as a failure and does not stop the drain. (2) Hestia's re-queue path and queue admission refuse a request that a person has closed. They record the refusal reason. Only an explicit reopen by a person lifts it. Acceptance: a test with a queue holding a paused-line item followed by a normal item shows drain runs the normal item and exits cleanly. A test shows a person-closed request is not re-queued by Hestia. A test shows the paused item runs again once the pause is lifted. Include the existing item 20261031-184832-4gah and request 0hmz as the starting point, and do not duplicate work already landed by them. Avoid banned words in any written text, and modify existing files where the code already exists.
